newsitem.title: USA: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS LOWER AFTER SLOW SESSION.
newsitem.headline: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS LOWER AFTER SLOW SESSION.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower after a thinly-traded session, and traders said commercial buying helped limit the kinds of losses seen in KCBT and CBOT wheat futures.

Wheat weakened early on spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans, which dropped sharply after beneficial rains fell over the weekend in dry growing areas of Illinois and Indiana. Meteorologists said more rain was forecast to hit the area through Tuesday.
But spring wheat values recovered from their lows thanks to a lack of selling and commercial-oriented buying.

"Atwood-Peavey did about 25 percent of the business in the pit today," a trader said. "They bought 1.6 million (December) and 800,000 March. It was so light that that's all it took to keep us relatively firm to Chicago."
Traders said volumes were light ahead of the scheduled release Tuesday of USDA's August crop report.
MGE spring wheat settled 1/2 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 1-3/4 cents at $3.96 a bushel.
The MGE estimated spring wheat futures volume Monday at 13.3 million bushels, down from 17.895 million Friday.
